title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 18-20). Section 7 sets up a dictionary between two kinds of data. On one side is a group extension 1 -> pi -> E -> G -> 1 together with a non-empty E-set Z on which pi acts freely. On the other side is a datum (Pi, Pi~, p, G, ~): a groupoid Pi with a universal covering Pi~ -> Pi and a group G acting compatibly. Concretely, E is the group of pairs (g, g~) and pi = Aut(Pi~/Pi). The motivating case is the arithmetic fundamental group of a curve: pi is the geometric (discrete or profinite) surface group, G is a Galois group, and E is the arithmetic pi_1.

Section 8, begun on p. 18, adds 'cusp data' (chi, C, T, Phi):
- C is an E-set (the cusps of the universal covering).
- T is a group, expected to be Z^ (the inertia).
- chi: G -> Aut(T) is expected to be the cyclotomic character G -> Z^*.
- Phi: C -> Hom_gr(T, pi) is E-equivariant.

This page first makes the equivariance explicit. E acts on C as given. It acts on Hom(T, pi) through two actions: on T through E -> G and chi; on pi by inner automorphisms (conjugation inside E). Grothendieck writes Sigma here for the group called E on p. 18.

He then sets J = C/pi, the set of cusps downstairs. The group G = Sigma/pi acts on J, and C -> J is Sigma-equivariant. He defines the groupoid <T, J>:
- its objects are J;
- Hom(J, J') is empty if J != J' and equals T if J = J';
- composition is the multiplication of T.
So <T, J> is the disjoint union, over J, of copies of BT. G acts on it through chi on T and through its action on J.

The goal announced is a G-morphism of groupoids <T, J> -> Pi^. Here Pi^ is the groupoid of universal coverings of Pi. Once one universal covering Pi~ is chosen, Pi^ is identified with the groupoid of pi-torsors, i.e. it is equivalent to B(pi).

The next page carries this out:
- each cusp class J goes to a pi-torsor P_J mapping to the fibre C_J;
- the stabiliser pi_t of t in C_J centralises Phi(t)(T);
- one then imposes the axiom that T is commutative and Phi_t: T -> pi_t is an isomorphism (cusp stabiliser = inertia group).

In modern terms this is a groupoid-theoretic encoding of a Galois-equivariant 'peripheral structure' on a surface group. It assigns to each cusp an inertia homomorphism Z^ -> pi_1, well defined up to conjugacy and twisted by the cyclotomic character. This is the combinatorial or anabelian 'paradigm' of a punctured algebraic curve over a field.
errors: Notational drift: the extension group is written E on p. 18 and Sigma on this page. Likewise 'J = C/pi' carries an inserted G, meaning G = Sigma/pi acts on it. These are the same objects.

The G-action on Pi^ (the groupoid of pi-torsors) is only defined up to the choice of lifts to E/Sigma, i.e. up to inner automorphisms of pi. So a 'G-morphism <T, J> -> Pi^' must be understood 2-categorically: pseudo-equivariance, with coherence data. A strict G-action on <T, J> matched against an action by autoequivalences on Pi^ needs this care, and the page does not address it.

On this page Phi is defined on C, which is not a pi-torsor, since pi acts on it with stabilisers. The passage from Phi to a torsor-valued functor is only completed on the next page, by adding the axiom Phi_t: T -> pi_t iso. As stated here the construction is still incomplete.

ideas.what: Dictionary between group extensions 1 -> pi -> E -> G -> 1 with an E-set, and groupoids with universal covering plus a compatible G-action (the groupoid of universal coverings being equivalent to pi-torsors)
ideas.modern_name: Galois descent / equivariant fundamental groupoids; outer actions as actions on B(pi)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 Galois theory) and the folklore of equivariant groupoids
ideas.where_published: Related material in SGA1 (exp. V) and in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (groupoïdes fondamentaux)

ideas.what: Cusp data (C, T ~ Z^, chi cyclotomic, Phi: C -> Hom(T, pi) equivariant), encoded as a G-morphism from a disjoint union of BT's (indexed by cusp classes J) to the groupoid of pi-torsors
ideas.modern_name: Galois-equivariant peripheral structure / cuspidal inertia subgroups of arithmetic fundamental groups; profinite group pairs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, Esquisse) for the program; later Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi-Mochizuki (cuspidal inertia); Deligne 1989 (tangential base points)
ideas.where_published: Inertia at cusps and the cyclotomic character are discussed in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The exact groupoid formalism here is not known to be published.

ideas.what: Axiom that the cusp stabiliser in pi equals the image of the inertia T ~ Z^ (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Cusp stabilisers = inertia subgroups (malnormal procyclic subgroups of a surface group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fuchsian groups); profinite version in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Mochizuki)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formalises the cusp/inertia structure of the arithmetic fundamental group of a punctured curve as an equivariant morphism of groupoids <T, J> -> Pi^. Here <T, J> is a disjoint union of copies of BT, one per cusp class, and Pi^ is the groupoid of pi-torsors. This is a functorial, groupoid-level version of a 'peripheral system', rather than the usual list of conjugacy classes of inertia subgroups. It is close in spirit to later group-pair and tangential-base-point formalisms, but stated with explicit Galois twisting by chi.
missed.quote: On va définir un G-morphisme de groupoïdes <T,J> -> Pi^ où Pi^ est le groupoïde des rev. universels de Pi
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor historical point. It documents that Grothendieck's 1980-81 'paradigms' already used an equivariant-groupoid encoding of cuspidal inertia. That anticipates themes of profinite group pairs and the cuspidal structures used in combinatorial anabelian geometry. It does not appear to be a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is foundational bookkeeping: equivariance conventions, the quotient J = C/pi, and the definition of the groupoid <T, J>. It sits within a program (arithmetic surface groups with cusp inertia and the cyclotomic character) that Grothendieck described in La Longue Marche and Esquisse. The groupoid packaging is a mildly interesting unpublished detail but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'grâce à [-?-]' — the crossed-out symbol is likely chi: T is made a Sigma-group via chi (through Sigma -> G).
The inserted '(γ↦χ)' after 'sur T' is more plausibly '(via χ)', i.e. G acts on T via chi.
'J = C/pi {+G+}' — the inserted letter is the G in the following line, 'sur lequel Sigma et = Sigma/pi = G opère par passage au quotient'.
'identifiables (via Pi~_t [?] qui est un ∈ Pi^)' is better read as 'identifiables (via Pi~, qui est un élément de Pi^) au groupoïde des pi-torseurs'.
The group written Sigma on this page is the extension group called E on p. 18.
